problem_text:
A logistics company must dispatch a technician to inspect eleven critical network nodes in a telecommunications grid. The nodes are positioned at the following geographical coordinates:

Node Alpha: Coordinates (109,174)  
Node Beta: Coordinates (56,155)  
Node Gamma: Coordinates (101,142)  
Node Delta: Coordinates (56,116)  
Node Epsilon: Coordinates (49,86)  
Node Zeta: Coordinates (155,26)  
Node Eta: Coordinates (155,21)  
Node Theta: Coordinates (81,82)  
Node Iota: Coordinates (137,116)  
Node Kappa: Coordinates (83,65)  
Node Lambda: Coordinates (7,133)

The fiber-optic cable distances, measured in kilometers, between each pair of operable nodes are precisely known:

Alpha to Gamma: 33.0 km  
Alpha to Delta: 78.6 km  
Alpha to Epsilon: 106.5 km  
Alpha to Zeta: 155.0 km  
Alpha to Eta: 159.8 km  
Alpha to Theta: 96.2 km  
Alpha to Iota: 64.4 km

Alpha to Lambda: 109.9 km  
Beta to Gamma: 46.8 km

Beta to Iota: 89.9 km

Beta to Lambda: 53.7 km  
Gamma to Delta: 52.0 km

Delta to Epsilon: 30.8 km

Zeta to Theta: 92.8 km  
Zeta to Iota: 91.8 km  
Zeta to Kappa: 81.9 km  
Zeta to Lambda: 182.6 km  
Eta to Theta: 95.9 km  
Eta to Iota: 96.7 km  
Eta to Kappa: 84.4 km  
Eta to Lambda: 185.6 km  
Theta to Iota: 65.5 km  
Theta to Kappa: 17.1 km  
Theta to Lambda: 89.9 km  
Iota to Kappa: 74.3 km  
Iota to Lambda: 131.1 km  
Kappa to Lambda: 102.0 km

Due to a permanent infrastructure failure, no direct cable link exists between Node Alpha and Node Beta. Furthermore, a critical routing protocol imposes that exactly one of two specific backup links must be utilized in the inspection circuit: either the connection between Node Beta and Node Gamma, or the connection between Node Gamma and Node Delta.

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel distance for a closed inspection route that visits every node exactly once before returning to the origin point.
